name: virtualization_inventory
description: List the VMs, the disk files they name, the snapshots and the datastores that configuration files and inventory exports say exist, from a directory or a list of files. It reads, from their public descriptions and no others: VMware .vmx and .vmsd and ESXi's vmInventory.xml; a libvirt domain XML (devices, disks, backing stores), domain snapshot XML and storage pool XML; a Proxmox VM or container configuration (/etc/pve/qemu-server/<id>.conf, with its snapshot sections; a [special:...] section, such as the cloud-init settings, is listed as special and not as a snapshot) and storage.cfg. A Hyper-V (.vmcx, .vmrs), VirtualBox (.vbox), OVF or VMware template or state file is recognised and listed as unsupported, never guessed at, and a file of no recognised kind is counted by extension. Every record carries its source file id and the line or XML element it came from; versions are the strings the files carry (hardware version, machine type), and what they mean for a release is not stated. A disk a configuration names is looked up only among the files given: `in_set` no is a statement about the set, a hypervisor storage volume is listed and not looked up, and a configuration entry does not show that a VM ran, still exists or was not deleted. A time is derived only where the file states an epoch (Proxmox snaptime, libvirt creationTime, UTC by definition); the two raw fields of a .vmsd are kept raw and not decoded. XML is read with every DOCTYPE and entity declaration refused and the element count and depth bounded; text is read a line at a time with a line cap (a line of 64 KiB or more is not read: it is counted, the file is partial and the first such line is named); the clock is read inside a file, so that one large file ends at max_seconds as a partial file; a file over max_file_bytes is named and not read; a file with more than 100000 records is partial and says so. An XML file in an encoding the reader does not know fails that file and the run goes on. A Proxmox configuration names its first 200 snapshot and special sections with their totals; every snapshot section is a row of snapshots, paged whole. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries; exit 0 means the engine ran, not that the examination is complete. SENSITIVE: a configuration can hold a console password, a cloud-init password, an SSH key or a user-data blob under a key this tool does not show: only a fixed list of keys is shown, every other key is counted, and the names (not values) of those that look like credentials are listed with their line, their section and the length of the value, in every section they sit in; a libvirt console password attribute is named to a cap of 200 and counted past it. SENSITIVE: every string the answer shows is judged by the field it fills, in three layers, with the boundary text that the Windows and macOS tools carry too (one text in all 16 carriers). (1) A name (VM, datastore, snapshot, storage, key), a path or file name, an identifier (GUID, VMFS volume id, naa./eui./t10./wwn- device id, VMware uuid, MAC, CID, number) and a simple value (an enum word, a version, a time) is shown only when it fits the plain grammar of its kind: letters of any script, digits, space and a short list of punctuation, at most 128 characters a name (a path is judged component by component), no user-info shape, no secret's name beside a value, and no chain of 16 or more characters made of random-looking pieces (a GUID, a hexadecimal id of up to 24 digits, a number of up to 18 digits and the well-formed ids of devices are plain; an iqn. or t10. id is shown as an id only when what it holds reads as a name, and a t10. serial of 17 or more hexadecimal digits is withheld); anything else is `<withheld N characters: reason>` (a path component by component), and its original goes to the values files only with write_text in a job. (2) Every other text (a host name, a description, an annotation, an audit action or actor, a message) is judged on a copy with invisible and formatting characters taken out and the escapes of such characters decoded: user-info up to the last `@`, token-shaped runs, prefixed tokens (ghp_, AKIA, glpat-, sk_live_, SG., AIza and others), a PEM key, a run of more than 18 digits, and the value after a name that says it is a secret (password, passwd, passphrase, pwd, secret, token, credential, api, access, account or private key, auth, pw, sig, sas, otp, psk; any case, glued or CamelCase) after `=` or `:`, after a flag that takes one (-password x, --token x, --api-key x, -auth x, set password x, enable secret x) and behind a placeholder (password=<redacted>x, or <redacted> x when x is built like a secret), in time linear in the length; a name or a path component that holds a secret's name and, glued or after a space, a value of 7 or more characters built like a secret (password-Zq7kP2mR, Token Zq7kP2mR) is withheld whole. In free text these shapes are still shown whole (2,000 random plants per shape, two samples of 1,000 with different seeds, with 95% Wilson bounds in the pack's changelog): `password-srv01-` and 8 characters, 100% in each of seven alphabets (at least 99.8%); with 14 base62 characters 63%, with 24 0.05%; `password-` and two groups of 4 characters, 100%; a glued `--master-key` and 8 lower-case letters 7.7%, 8 hexadecimal digits 0.8%, 8 base62 characters 0.2%, 14 or 24 base62 characters none in 2,000. (3) The serialised answer, every error answer and every paging-file row are read back and checked by a second check written apart from the first two; a string it finds suspect, or in which it finds a piece of a secret-shaped text that the first two left between two cuts, is replaced by <withheld N bytes: backstop: why>, its place is listed in boundary.replaced_at, and the answer is partial. The judging of one run shares a cap of 400 million characters and a time that ends 6.5 seconds after max_seconds: past either, a string not judged before is withheld by its size (a short plain word stays readable), the answer is partial and boundary.stopped_by names the stop. A SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP that arrives once the module has run as far as its shared opening blocks (before any argument is read and before any evidence is touched) ends the tool with one JSON answer (status partial, stopped_by_signal naming the signal) and exit status 128 plus the signal number, the answer being a shorter one that says so if the signal comes before the output block has loaded; one that arrives earlier, while the interpreter starts and compiles the file and runs those blocks, gets no answer. Only the exact names of the files this run made are shown as they are; an extension that is not 1 to 10 letters or digits is counted under (other extensions). A short password used as a name, a token under 16 characters in a name, a value of 6 characters or fewer after a secret's name, a value built like words, a name the grammar of a plain name refuses (it is withheld: a false positive), and the shapes listed with their measured rates in the pack's changelog are not recognised, so run as a job with secret_output: true. write_text: true (refused outside a job) creates two files under $OUT, mode 0600, both created before anything is read: inventory-values.jsonl (the original of every name or value shown withheld or shortened) and virtualization_inventory-values.jsonl (the original of every string the boundary withheld or replaced, one JSON line each: id, field, label, length, value); a file already there is refused by name.  A name, a path, a URL or a message that quotes a credential is withheld with the identifier-shaped strings, from version 8: a value given to a password, token, secret or cookie name (password=..., Pwd=..., a Cookie header), a Name/Value pair in text whose Name is a credential (a number, an array or a long Value too, and the NewValue after an OldValue), a -Password style switch, the argument of ConvertTo-SecureString, curl -u user:pass, mysql -uUSER -pSECRET, a bcrypt hash and the known token families; the text is replaced by a marker that holds only its length. Before, only identifier-shaped strings (tokens, key ids, user-info) were withheld, so these were printed. Known gaps: a pair whose Value is an array nested in another or longer than 4,096 characters, a crypt hash that is not bcrypt, and a secret that has neither a credential name nor a token shape.

root.description: A directory of the evidence files (a link is refused; links inside it are listed and never followed). Give root, paths, or both

paths.description: Files named one by one (a link or a special file is named and never opened)

limit.description: Rows shown inline per list (default 200); every row is counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results; the rows shown inline also stop at about 512 KiB per list whatever limit says (pages.<list>.inline_cut_by_size), so that the answer is written within max_seconds and keeps its status: the rest is in the file

max_files.description: The most files taken into the set (default 20000, at most 200000); past it the answer is partial and says where the walk stopped

max_entries.description: The most directory entries listed (default 200000, at most 2000000)

max_depth.description: How deep the walk goes (default 16, at most 64); a deeper directory is named

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 50, at most 50); what is left is named and the answer is partial

write_text.description: Write the original of every name or value the answer shows withheld or shortened to 0600 files under $OUT (the tool's own text file and virtualization_inventory-values.jsonl) (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job that is secret output: the manifest declares it, so a job with write_text true is made secret by the job service whether or not the agent asked

max_file_bytes.description: A file over this many bytes is named and not read (default 16777216, at most 268435456); nothing is cut
